input.prompt:
Explore the external vsim repo at /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim (sources) with prebuilt engines in /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build (binaries named sim_*, e.g. sim_ax45mpv_premium). This is a SystemC + Verilator cycle-accurate Andes RISC-V simulator ("vsim") that models an AE350-like platform. Search breadth: very thorough.

GOAL: audit the existing `--print-memmap` CLI option for correctness, and independently establish the simulator's REAL address decode from source.

Tasks:
1. Find where the CLI option `--print-memmap` (or print_memmap / memmap) is parsed and implemented. Report file:line and QUOTE the code that emits each region (name, base, size). Determine where the region list comes from: hardcoded literals? config macros (config.inc / NDS_* defines)? generated? Does it vary per engine build?
2. Independently establish the ACTUAL platform address decode from source: how the SystemC top / bus / interconnect routes addresses. Enumerate every mapped region with base+size and file:line evidence: main RAM (base? size? how set?), ILM/DLM slave-port apertures, HVM/subordinate port, UART (expect ~0xf0300000), SimControl/HTIF (expect ~0xe0080000), L2C MMIO (expect ~0xE0500000), PLIC/PLICSW, PLMT, Debug Module, SMU, anything else. Note which regions exist conditionally (e.g. only when the engine config has ILM/DLM/L2C/HVM).
3. Check built engine configs: list the sim_* binaries in /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build, and for sim_ax45mpv_premium (and one other if present, e.g. an ax66 engine) find its generated config at build/**/obj_sc/config.inc (or similar) and extract memory-relevant macros: ILM/DLM size+base, HVM size, _NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB, RAM/mem size, VLEN, NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS.
4. Try RUNNING (read-only, use `timeout 30`): `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium --print-memmap`, also `--describe` and `--help`. Capture output VERBATIM. If a run is blocked by permissions or hangs, just note it and move on.

- Note (2026-06-12 retitle): 128 MB is only the DEFAULT, not the limit.
  `--mem-size` sets the program RAM up to 2 GiB - 4 KiB; the driver maps that
  PLUS one 4 KiB V-transport scratch page on top (L26), so mmap = QEMU memory
  backend = vsim RAM window. The old title "must fit in the 128 MB shared
  mmap" was misleading. The real limitation is now the RUNTIME-growth fit
  check plus the 2 GiB ceiling.
- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the size in
  effect (default 128 MB), or the workload needs more than 2 GiB at all.
- What happens: the STATIC image is now checked -- a load-time guard
  (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`, L26/F3) rejects an ELF whose PT_LOAD
  segments reach past `--mem-size` (into the reserved scratch page) with a
  clear "raise --mem-size" message. But RUNTIME growth (heap or stack past
  the ceiling) still has no startup check: vsim's memory rejects or truncates
  the access, QEMU may see it as MMIO, and nothing names `--mem-size` as the
  cause. Separately, 2 GiB is a hard wall: the AE350 DRAM window is
  `0x00000000..0x80000000`, QEMU rejects a larger `ram_size`, and the driver
  pre-caps `--mem-size` at 2 GiB - 4 KiB (the window minus the scratch page)
  -- no setting runs a > 2 GiB workload.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:414` (128 MB default), `:424` (2 GiB - 4 KiB
  pre-cap), `:440-455` (the L26/F3 static-image guard, via `driver/elf_syms.hpp`
  `elf_load_top`); `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c` (DRAM window + ram_size
  check); `src/main.cpp` (vsim RAM window sized from
  `--shared-mem-size`).
- Status: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED. The static PT_LOAD fit check landed (L26/F3)
  and the V scratch can no longer be clobbered (it moved above program RAM,
  L26); runtime heap/stack overflow past the ceiling still corrupts silently.
  Workaround: pass `--mem-size` large enough by hand (USER_GUIDE 2.5);
  > 2 GiB workloads cannot run.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. Resuming
  hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI: only the vplat device set is handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches any device OTHER than the vplat set - PLIC,
  the timer (`mtime`/`mtimecmp`), ROM, or aliased/device memory - or expects
  device STATE to survive the handoff.
- What happens: UART2 (`0xf0300000`) and SimControl/HTIF (`0xe0080000`) are
  modeled by BOTH engines (QEMU: `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` + the ae350
  memmap; vsim: the AE350 RTL platform natively), so vplat stdio / exit /
  file io inside the ROI work and the hybrid leg relays vsim's UART output.
  Any other device range is engine-specific behavior. And no device state
  (UART FIFO contents, pending interrupts, timer compare) crosses the
  handoff - only RAM is shared; each engine has its own device instances.
- Where: `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:95,107` (SimControl + UART2 memmap);
  `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`.
- Status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (2026-06): vplat device set works; everything
  else and cross-handoff device state still OPEN."

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.

  hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI: only the vplat device set is handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches any device OTHER than the vplat set - PLIC,

- What happens: UART2 (`0xf0300000`) and SimControl/HTIF (`0xe0080000`) are
  modeled by BOTH engines (QEMU: `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` + the ae350
  memmap; vsim: the AE350 RTL platform natively), so vplat stdio / exit /
  file io inside the ROI work and the hybrid leg relays vsim's UART output.
  Any other device range is engine-specific behavior. And no device state
  (UART FIFO contents, pending interrupts, timer compare) crosses the
  handoff - only RAM is shared; each engine has its own device instances.
- Where: `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:95,107` (SimControl + UART2 memmap);
  `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`.
